# Plan 01-02: Antialiased waveshaper

## Goal
Drive audibly saturates with aliasing below -80 dBFS and no perceived loudness change.

## Context
`Source/dsp/` holds header-only, JUCE-free DSP classes. Add the shaper there so it can be
unit tested without the plugin. `Source/PluginProcessor.cpp` calls it in processBlock.

## Tasks

<task id="1">
  <name>ADAA tanh waveshaper</name>
  <files>Source/dsp/Shaper.h</files>
  <action>Header-only first-order antiderivative antialiased tanh. Keep the previous input
  sample as state. Guard the near-zero denominator with a fallback to the direct tanh —
  do not let it divide by a value close to zero.</action>
  <verify>ctest --test-dir build -R Aliasing --output-on-failure</verify>
  <fails_when>non-zero exit, or the measured alias floor is above -80 dBFS</fails_when>
  <done>1 kHz sine at full drive measures below -80 dBFS of aliasing</done>
</task>

<task id="2">
  <name>Gain compensation</name>
  <files>Source/PluginProcessor.cpp</files>
  <action>Apply post-shaper compensation derived from the pre-gain. Compensate once, in
  one place — never both before and after the shaper.</action>
  <verify>ctest --test-dir build -R Loudness</verify>
  <fails_when>non-zero exit, or the LU spread across the drive range exceeds 1.0</fails_when>
  <done>Loudness across 0..100% drive stays within 1 LU</done>
</task>

## Must-haves
- [ ] Aliasing below -80 dBFS at full drive
- [ ] Loudness within 1 LU across the drive range

## Try it
Build the standalone, sweep Drive with a 1 kHz sine playing, and confirm it gets dirtier
without getting louder.
